$comment: AP6 / plan 06 §5.1 B.13.3 — a `module` PROJECT BUILT STANDALONE, which before that ruling was a REJECTED build. `artifactProfile: "module"` is the only profile whose whole prior existence was as something a consumer absorbs; B.13.3 ruled that a module IS a library, served by every object format that serves `lib` or `staticlib` and by nothing else, so a module project emits a real artifact of its own like any other library. This manifest is that claim in its smallest honest form: one module, no consumer, four targets, one archive each.
$commentProfileVsComposition: ★ `artifactProfile` AND `DependencyComposition` ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS, and this file only answers the first. `artifactProfile` says what a project builds ITSELF as (here: a library, in whatever container the target spec names). `DependencyComposition` says how a project is CONSUMED — and `module`'s verb is SourceMerge (core/types/artifact_profile.hpp), so a consumer that depends on this directory takes its SOURCES and ignores the archive built here entirely. The two are ORTHOGONAL, which is exactly why this build is legal and why no example needs to link its output: `examples/c/project_dependson_module_source_merge` is the consumed half, and it asserts the module's own artifact ABSENT. Neither example is the other's duplicate.
$commentWhyStaticlibSpecs: The static-vs-dynamic choice is made by the `<target>:<format>` spec written below, NEVER by the profile name — the same division `lib` and `staticlib` already use, which is why `module` needed no new engine mechanism to become buildable. `-staticlib` formats are chosen here because `container: "archive"` is the one output shape that is meaningful for all four platforms without a link step, an entry point, or a runtime loader: the driver routes each CU's relocatable member into ONE `ar` archive via linkAndWriteStaticArchive, dispatching on the format's `container` field and never on the profile name (the artifact_profile.hpp veto).
$commentTargetsAreAllFour: All four platform legs are listed because the capability under test is not 'a module builds' but 'a module builds ON EVERY LEG'. The in-process corpus runner compiles every declared target on every host, so this list is what turns a one-host unit pin into a cross-leg witness — see expected.json for the full argument and for why nothing here is ever spawned.
